articles.title: You’ve Been Mogged. There’s a Scientific Reason It Feels So Bad.
articles.summary: Mogging, a term popularized by looksmaxxers like Clavicular, describes a complicated phenomenon of social comparison. Here, experts explain the science behin...
articles.body:
AT SIX-FOOT-FOUR , I'm not accustomed to feeling physically dwarfed. Sure, I might not have bulging muscles—but I confess I occasionally survey the other men in the gym and entertain the idea that I might be the hottest guy in the room. Sometimes, though, a bigger, better looking dude walks in and starts lifting heavier weights than me. My confidence evaporates, along with, I imagine, the admiring glances of all the men and women (who, on reflection, might not actually have been paying me any mind).

Until recently, I didn't have a name for this peculiar, perhaps Palaeolithic phenomenon. Mogging, derived from "alpha M ale O f the G roup," describes the act of one man outshining another, through any combination of height, muscularity, facial attractiveness, status, or charisma (a.k.a. "aura"). On the receiving end, it's the sudden, visceral realization that another man might be stronger or better-looking than you, and the cascade of feelings of inferiority that follow.

"To mog" entered the lexicon thanks to figures like Braden Peters, better known as Clavicular. The 20-year-old looksmaxxing influencer was spectacularly "frame-mogged" on his own livestream in a viral moment earlier this year. The curious phrasing captured online attention, and on November 3 "mogging" was crowned Collins Dictionary's word of the year for 2026.

But this type of social scenario didn't just emerge with the dawn of the internet. I was curious: Does this emasculating sensation stem from an ancient status instinct, an ego threat, a form of social comparison, or something else? And why are some men so sensitive to it?

THIS ISSUE OF mogging raises a question: Why should another man's stature have such an immediate effect on my self-esteem ? It's a theme explored in the classics. In Homer's Iliad , the ancient Greek epic, King Priam spots the enormous warrior Ajax, "whose head and shoulders tower above the rest." Yet Homer also understood that size wasn't everything. Earlier in the same passage, Menelaus is described as broader-shouldered than Odysseus, the cunning hero played by Matt Damon in The Odyssey —but the shorter man's extraordinary eloquence renders his stature irrelevant.

Modern researchers have also looked for answers. Human judgment "is by nature comparative" and social comparisons are "spontaneous, effortless, and unintentional reactions to the performance of others," according to a 2014 review of the early indications on the brain mechanisms of social comparison and their influence on the reward system.

Meanwhile, other related research found that physically stronger men were perceived as having higher social status, partly because they were considered more capable leaders. But does this make the discomfort of being mogged inevitable?

Psychologists distinguish between dominance , in which status is secured through intimidation, and prestige , which is earned through the admiration of others. Research suggests that even if the strongest and most attractive may initially draw outsized attention, or mog, prestige is ultimately conferred upon those who benefit the group , rather than pursue aggressive self-interest.

For couples therapist Sarah Tilley, this dynamic reflects the tension between our instinctive deference to appearances and our recognition of its limitations. Snap judgments of competence from candidates' faces predicted almost 69 percent of US senate races in 2004, according to a study in Science

"There is a deference to beauty and we're all culprits," she says. "Beauty trumps intelligence, but only for a short amount of time. Smart people will know that, but it takes wisdom." In other words, the actual effects of a mog could be fleeting if there is someone smarter in the room.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY happening when you feel the mog? Turns out, there are chemical responses behind those feelings of self-doubt.

"A review of more than 200 lab studies found that our cortisol is reliably spiked when we feel that others are judging us and when we can't control the outcome," says Dr Manesh Girn, a neuroscientist and men's work facilitator.

"Envy toward someone who outranks you on something you care about also activates the anterior cingulate cortex, a region tied to processing pain and conflict," he says, citing a study on the neural correlates of envy and schadenfreude (the feeling of satisfaction when someone faces consequences they deserve).

But the susceptibility to feeling mogged also depends on one's values and sense of self-worth. "Shorter men are more sensitive than taller men to dominance cues in other men's faces and voices," adds Girn. In the envy study, pain responses only arose when the other person's perceived superiority was in a domain the participant particularly cared about.

Looksmaxxer-in-chief Peters admitted last month that he now simply removes himself from social settings when there's a possibility he might be mogged. "It really has a soul-crushing effect," he told podcaster Patrick Bet-David, recalling a recent weight room encounter. "We just felt the mog from all the way across the gym to the point where I just left. Why would I want that internal pressure?"

Such an extreme reaction suggests "a maladaptive mindset," says Charlotte Markey, a professor of psychology at Rutgers University. "Social comparison is a very normal process, including in terms of our physical attributes."

For some men in 2026, that drives an obsession to become the strongest of the pack. This can become genuinely debilitating.

"I've cared for young people who then go to the gym five plus hours a day, and it starts to detract from their quality of life," says Jason Nagata, an associate professor of pediatrics at the University of California, San Francisco, who researches male body image. "The concern is when self-improvement becomes self-worth, because it becomes dependent on outperforming someone else."

And while this might be driven by instinct, the experts caution against succumbing to our baser instincts. "It may be evolutionarily baked in," says Markey, "but we want to be careful not to oversimplify here. We aren't cavemen."

Would You Spend 5 Hours a Day in the Gym to Avoid the Mog?

HOWEVER, THE CAVEMAN is not quite dead. We form impressions of a face within a tenth of a second , and people can estimate a man's upper body strength from his face alone. For our ancestors, misjudging who could beat them in a fight may have been a costly mistake. Some research suggests that our sensitivity to physical formidability reflects this ancient pressure, which may help explain why strength continues to influence perceptions of status.

Despite sometimes feeling the mog (and after injuries that prevent heavy lifting), I'm generally content to stick to lighter weights in the gym rather than packing on mass to stand out more in a room. Yet I wonder whether my own instinctive competitiveness has affected my relationships with other men. If I'm constantly assessing where I stand in some invisible hierarchy, like a dog jostling for position in its pack, surely it becomes more difficult to strike up friendships.

In a 2017 study of 100 physically active young men, researchers found that those at risk of muscle dysmorphia were less inclined to socialize than their peers, potentially due to social comparison tendencies. The pursuit of the perfect physique, it seems, can come at the expense of the very relationships it might be intended to improve.

SO WHY, AFTER millennia of social comparison, do we have this very modern understanding of the mogging dynamic? Social media has transformed what was once a largely local competition into a global one, exposing men to an endless parade of gorgeous bodies and faces against which to measure themselves (albeit at lower rates than women). "The Greeks didn't compare themselves with the best, idealized versions of everyone in the world," says Nagata.

Indeed, researchers effectively recreated the experience of being mogged in a study involving 300 men aged 18 to 30. They were randomly assigned to view images of bare-chested and muscular men alongside clothed photos and pictures of scenery. Exposure to the half-naked Chads resulted in significantly lower body satisfaction.

I would never flee a gym or a bar upon the entrance of a potentially more attractive man. But back in April—shortly after mogging entered my lexicon—I couldn't help noticing how much attention a very handsome (and very muscular) longtime male friend was receiving. One woman I didn't even know basically cat-called him on the street and complimented his outfit. Naturally I assessed my own. It wasn't nearly as cool, I lamented.

Now, after years of feeling this mysterious, disempowering sensation in his company without entirely being able to place it, I had a name for my predicament: I'd been mogged. Still, I was able to keep it together. We enjoyed our lunch, and we remain friends.

Perhaps the instinct to compare ourselves is unavoidable . Sometimes I wonder whether the worst thing about discovering mogging is becoming conscious of a competition I never even realized I was in.

articles.title: Trump diz que há chance 'muito boa' de acordo sobre guerra na Ucrânia | G1
articles.standfirst: Apesar do otimismo, o presidente dos EUA evitou discutir possíveis garantias de segurança para a Ucrânia antes de um acordo de paz mais amplo.
articles.summary: Apesar do otimismo, o presidente dos EUA evitou discutir possíveis garantias de segurança para a Ucrânia antes de um acordo de paz mais amplo.
articles.body:
Donald Trump e Vladimir Putin. — Foto: Kevin Lamarque/Reuters

O presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump , afirmou nesta sexta-feira (20) que teve conversas "muito boas" com o líder russo, Vladimir Putin , sobre a guerra na Ucrânia e que vê boas chances de um acordo para encerrar o conflito.

"Estamos tendo conversas muito boas. Acho que há uma chance muito boa de conseguirmos chegar a um acordo", disse Trump em entrevista coletiva na Casa Branca, após retornar de uma viagem à Ásia.

O presidente americano se reuniu com Putin nesta semana, durante o encontro da Cooperação Econômica Ásia-Pacífico (Apec), em Shenzhen, na China. Na ocasião, também esteve com o presidente chinês, Xi Jinping.

Segundo Trump, Putin, a quem chamou de amigo , demonstrou interesse em encerrar a guerra por meio de negociações.

"Ele expressou claramente seu desejo de ver a guerra entre Rússia e Ucrânia terminar por meios diplomáticos. E conversei com nossos representantes, que estão fazendo um bom trabalho, mas é um trabalho difícil", afirmou Trump.

Apesar do otimismo, Trump evitou discutir as garantias de segurança para a Ucrânia, um dos principais impasses das negociações. "Não quero falar sobre garantias porque precisamos chegar a um acordo primeiro", afirmou.

Na quinta-feira (19), Jared Kushner, conselheiro e genro de Trump, afirmou que o presidente americano estava aberto a oferecer à Ucrânia garantias de segurança semelhantes às previstas na Organização do Tratado do Atlântico Norte (Otan).

A proposta seguiria o princípio do Artigo 5º da aliança militar, segundo o qual um ataque contra um país-membro é considerado um ataque contra todos.

Após negociações em Berlim, Kushner também disse acreditar que os russos estavam "confortáveis com esse conceito".

A Rússia, porém, rejeitou a possibilidade. Nesta sexta-feira, o vice-ministro das Relações Exteriores, Sergei Ryabkov, afirmou que qualquer forma de "quase adesão" da Ucrânia à Otan seria totalmente inaceitável para Moscou, segundo a imprensa estatal russa.

Questionado sobre as declarações contraditórias, Trump atribuiu a divergência às estratégias de negociação.

"Olha, nosso lado divulga certas coisas porque também é uma guerra de relações públicas. Nós dizemos coisas, e eles dizem coisas", afirmou. "Só posso dizer que o presidente Putin gostaria de resolver isso, e disso tenho certeza."

Apesar das declarações sobre um possível acordo de paz, os ataques russos continuam.

Horas depois de Trump, Putin e Xi Jinping divulgarem uma declaração conjunta de paz após o encontro na China, a Rússia lançou um dos maiores ataques com mísseis e drones desde o início da guerra, em fevereiro de 2022.

articles.title: Decoração de Natal vira atração em Itaperuna | G1
articles.standfirst: Enfeites e luzes montados por morador do distrito de Raposo chamam a atenção de turistas e moradores; expectativa é de aumento no fluxo de visitantes durante o feriado prolongado.
articles.summary: Enfeites e luzes montados por morador do distrito de Raposo chamam a atenção de turistas e moradores; expectativa é de aumento no fluxo de visitantes durante o feriado prolongado.
articles.body:
Uma casa decorada para o Natal tem chamado a atenção de moradores e turistas em Raposo, distrito de Itaperuna , no Norte Fluminense. A decoração, que reúne cerca de 6 mil lâmpadas de LED, foi montada pelo guia de turismo Bruno Martins , com o objetivo de incentivar outras pessoas a enfeitarem suas residências e resgatar a tradição natalina.

Bruno conta que decidiu investir na decoração para estimular o espírito natalino na comunidade.

“Minha intenção é chamar a atenção das pessoas para que elas também enfeitem as casas. A gente percebe que as pessoas estão perdendo um pouco da magia do Natal”, afirma.

Durante o feriado prolongado, a expectativa é que muitos visitantes passem pelo local para tirar fotos e gravar vídeos. Segundo Bruno, Raposo deve receber pelo menos 23 ônibus de turismo no período.

Ao longo dos anos, o guia turístico aperfeiçoou a montagem dos enfeites e criou um sistema próprio para facilitar a instalação e o funcionamento das luzes.

“Hoje faço tudo com um fio só. Consigo ligar tudo por um interruptor, sem precisar ir ligando um por um”, explica.

A decoração reúne pisca-piscas de 50 metros, incluindo modelos do tipo estrobo. Os enfeites são fixados com parafusos para evitar que se soltem ou fiquem embolados em dias de vento. Bruno também destaca que a iluminação não gera um aumento significativo na conta de energia elétrica.

“No ano passado, só aumentou R$ 50 na conta. Eu não deixo as luzes ligadas a noite toda”, afirma.

A decoração ainda está em fase de conclusão. Nos próximos dias, ele pretende acrescentar um Papai Noel, uma guirlanda e outros enfeites.

articles.title: Mosca-da-bicheira: Casos aumentam nos EUA e ameaçam rebanhos | G1
articles.standfirst: Parasita devora animais de sangue quente vivos e ameaça o rebanho bovino. Pecuaristas temem que os casos continuem a aumentar devido à escassez de moscas estéreis criadas para combater a praga.
articles.summary: A mosca-da-bicheira atingiu 64 animais em novembro nos EUA; autoridades locais correm para ampliar a produção de moscas estéreis e conter o avanço do parasita no país.
articles.body:
Duas moscas-da-bicheira do Novo Mundo no Laboratório de Pesquisa de Insetos Pecuários Knipling-Bushland, em Kerrville, Texas, EUA. — Foto: REUTERS/Kaylee Greenlee

Os surtos nos Estados Unidos (EUA) da chamada mosca-da-bicheira do Novo Mundo aumentaram drasticamente devido ao clima excepcionalmente úmido e quente no sudoeste do país.

As informações são do Departamento de Agricultura dos EUA (USDA) e veterinários estaduais. O parasita devora animais de sangue quente vivos e ameaça o rebanho bovino.

A mosca-da-bicheira infestou 64 bovinos, cães, cavalos e outros animais domesticados neste mês, um aumento em relação aos 34 casos registrados em outubro e aos três em setembro, segundo dados do USDA.

O departamento registrou um total de 149 casos em animais domesticados desde junho, além de dois em alces selvagens. Desses, 73 casos estavam ativos até quinta-feira, um aumento em relação aos dois registrados no final de setembro.

Pecuaristas temem que os casos continuem a aumentar devido à escassez de moscas estéreis criadas para combater as moscas-da-bicheira.

“O enxame ainda não chegou ao Texas”, disse Susan Storey, uma pecuarista do sul do Texas.

O USDA corre para ampliar a capacidade de produção de moscas estéreis, com o Corpo de Engenheiros do Exército supervisionando a construção de uma fábrica de moscas no sul do Texas, com inauguração prevista para o próximo ano.

O subsecretário do USDA, Dudley Hoskins, disse à agência de notícias Reuters que um projeto para testar moscas estéreis geneticamente modificadas -- que poderiam ajudar na resposta -- está em andamento.

O departamento detectou pela primeira vez a mosca-da-bicheira em um bezerro no Texas em junho, após o parasita avançar para o norte por meio do México, e posteriormente confirmou mais casos no Texas e no Novo México. Depois de um período de calmaria, a mosca-da-bicheira se espalhou no mês passado para o Arizona, que agora tem nove casos ativos em quatro condados.

As moscas-da-bicheira invadiram o Arizona pelo sul e pelo leste, disse o Dr. Ryan Wolker, veterinário estadual.

“O principal fator contribuinte é a progressão natural da praga e o suprimento limitado de moscas-da-bicheira machos estéreis”, afirmou ele.

O USDA está liberando todas as moscas estéreis disponíveis no sudoeste dos EUA e ao redor da fronteira norte do México para conter as infestações, enquanto o parasita continua se multiplicando mais ao sul. Os machos estéreis acasalam com fêmeas selvagens, cujos ovos, então, não eclodem.

Pesquisadores no Panamá avançaram nos testes com moscas estéreis geneticamente modificadas para produzir apenas machos, o que poderia dar ao USDA uma vantagem na batalha contra as moscas-da-bicheira, disse Hoskins.

As moscas, conhecidas como NovoFly, poderiam dobrar a produção de moscas estéreis ao eliminar as fêmeas, que não são úteis nos esforços de erradicação, afirmou ele.

“Até o momento, todos os sinais indicam progresso e uma forte competitividade da NovoFly na natureza”, disse Hoskins. “Os testes realizados até agora demonstraram tudo o que esperávamos que demonstrassem.”

O USDA pretende produzir a NovoFly nas instalações com inauguração prevista para abril no Texas, caso os testes continuem a correr bem, disse Hoskins. Ele acrescentou que levará tempo para aumentar a produção.

articles.title: Copa do Mundo Feminina 2027: Bahia terá suspensão de aulas | G1
articles.standfirst: Resolução do Conselho Estadual de Educação prevê paralisação das atividades letivas em todo o estado nos dias de jogos da Seleção Brasileira e, em Salvador, também nas partidas realizadas na Arena Acelen Fonte Nova.
articles.summary: A Copa do Mundo Feminina 2027 terá suspensão de aulas na Bahia em dias de jogos do Brasil e partidas em Salvador, com reposição obrigatória do calendário letivo.
articles.body:
Seleção Brasileira não vai jogar na Arena Fonte Nova, mas as aulas serão suspensas em dias de jogos de outras seleções em Salvador. — Foto: Eric Luis Carvalho/g1

As escolas da Bahia não terão aulas nos dias de jogos da Seleção Brasileira durante a Copa do Mundo Feminina de 2027 . A orientação foi aprovada pelo Conselho Estadual de Educação da Bahia e publicada no Diário Oficial do Estado desta sexta-feira (20).

A medida valerá para todas as instituições integrantes do Sistema Estadual de Ensino, incluindo escolas públicas e privadas, em todos os municípios baianos.

Além disso, em Salvador , também não haverá atividades letivas nos dias em que a Arena Acelen Fonte Nova receber partidas da competição, independentemente das seleções em campo.

Segundo a resolução, a suspensão das aulas valerá para todos os turnos, níveis e modalidades de ensino da rede estadual, incluindo educação básica, educação profissional técnica de nível médio e cursos de qualificação profissional.

Os dias sem aulas não serão contabilizados como dias letivos. Por isso, as instituições de ensino deverão realizar a reposição das atividades para garantir o cumprimento do mínimo de 200 dias letivos anuais exigidos pela Lei de Diretrizes e Bases da Educação Nacional (LDB).

No caso da educação profissional técnica e dos cursos de qualificação profissional, a reposição deverá assegurar o cumprimento integral da carga horária prevista em cada curso.

A resolução também permite que as escolas organizem o período de férias do primeiro semestre de 2027 de forma a coincidir total ou parcialmente com a realização da competição.

Além disso, as unidades de ensino deverão informar previamente à comunidade escolar sobre os dias de suspensão e as datas definidas para reposição, registrando essas informações no calendário escolar antes do início do ano letivo.

Em parecer que fundamentou a decisão, o Conselho Estadual de Educação recomenda que as escolas desenvolvam atividades pedagógicas relacionadas ao futebol feminino, à igualdade de gênero e às experiências das mulheres na sociedade.

A proposta segue diretrizes da legislação federal que incentiva ações educacionais voltadas à valorização do esporte feminino e à promoção da equidade de gênero no ambiente escolar.

A resolução foi aprovada pelo Conselho Estadual de Educação em sessão realizada em Vitória da Conquista e homologada pelo secretário estadual da Educação em 18 de novembro de 2026.

articles.title: Praia da Ponta Negra é interditada após Rio Negro baixar de 16m | G1
articles.standfirst: Medida foi anunciada pela Prefeitura de Manaus nesta sexta-feira (20). Nível do rio Negro ficou abaixo da cota de 16 metros considerada de risco para a atividade.
articles.summary: Praia da Ponta Negra é interditada em Manaus após o Rio Negro atingir 15,94 metros, nível que oferece riscos de acidentes por buracos e depressões no leito do rio.
articles.body:
Praia da Ponta Negra é interditada devido à seca em Manaus — Foto: Divulgação/Semcom

A praia da Ponta Negra, na Zona Oeste de Manaus , foi interditada para banho nesta sexta-feira (20) devido ao baixo nível do rio Negro. Segundo a Prefeitura de Manaus, o nível do rio chegou a 15,94 metros.

A medida foi adotada pelo Instituto Municipal de Planejamento Urbano (Implurb), seguindo recomendação do Serviço Geológico do Brasil (SGB). O órgão considera o nível abaixo de 16 metros uma condição de risco para o banho.

De acordo com o SGB, com a água abaixo dessa marca, podem ocorrer alterações no leito do rio, como buracos, desníveis e depressões, que oferecem risco à segurança de banhistas. Por isso, a Prefeitura de Manaus orienta que frequentadores do complexo turístico da Ponta Negra se atente à sinalização e não entre na água para evitar acidentes.

A interdição é somente à área do rio, e permanecerá em vigor até que as condições hidrológicas e de segurança sejam normalizadas, conforme avaliação técnica do Implurb.

articles.title: Raio quebra vidro de janela e queima roupas no varal em Matias Barbosa | G1
articles.standfirst: Na Policlínica da cidade, telefone e internet ficaram inoperantes. “Achei que a nossa casa ia cair”, relatou moradora, que teve TV e outros aparelhos eletrônicos danificados.
articles.summary: Na Policlínica da cidade, telefone e internet ficaram inoperantes. “Achei que a nossa casa ia cair”, relatou moradora, que teve TV e outros aparelhos eletrônicos danificados.
articles.body:
Um temporal acompanhando de raios que passou em Matias Barbosa causou estragos em ao menos duas residências e assustou moradores, que relatam ter vivido momentos de apreensão na madrugada desta sexta-feira (20).

Em um dos imóveis, na Rua José Pedro Ribeiro Junqueira, no Bairro Maria Célia, os vidros da janela de um cômodo que fica no terceiro andar ficaram quebrados. Um vídeo mostra como ficou o local. Assista acima.

“Estava trovejando muito e dando uns clarões, sabe? Aí simplesmente deu um estouro. Parecia que caiu alguma coisa em cima da nossa casa. Levantei correndo da cama e falei com a minha mãe, que subiu e viu que a janela estava totalmente quebrada e trincada. De manhã a gente foi ver e estava tudo revirado, a parede do lado de dentro toda queimada”, relatou a moradora Andressa Lage.

Conforme Andressa, nem ela e nem a mãe, que moram no segundo andar, sofreram ferimentos. O que as assustou foi o barulho do raio.

“Choque eu não senti, mas senti que estava caindo uma coisa muito forte”.

O relógio de energia desarmou e, de acordo com ela, depois que elas conseguiram religa-lo, perceberam que alguns aparelhos eletrônicos foram danificados, como lâmpadas, um aparelho de TV, roteador de internet e pisca-pisca de Natal.

“A gente nunca viu uma coisa dessa aqui. Agora é correr atrás do prejuízo dos aparelhos queimados. Mas o susto foi o pior, porque eu achei que a nossa casa ia cair, de verdade”.

A janela ficou danificada e parte do vidro foi quebrada — Foto: Andressa Lage

Em outro ponto da cidade, na Rua Barão de Santa Helena, Bairro Santa Terezinha, a cerca de 15km da casa de Andressa, a moradora Emma Cristina Carnevali também acordou assustada na madrugada.

Na casa dela, roupas que estavam no varal na área externa ficaram queimadas. Veja nas fotos abaixo .

Raio caiu, e roupas que estavam no varal ficaram queimadas em Matias Barbosa — Foto: Emma Cristina Carnevali

“Estava eu minha filha, meu pai e minha irmã. Levamos muito susto. Teve um clarão e parecia que as luzes da casa estavam todas acessas. As roupas ficaram todas queimadas”.

Conforme ela, a máquina de lavar e o modem da internet foram queimados. “A televisão não estava funcionando, mas troquei a fonte e ela ligou”.

Conforme a Prefeitura de Matias Barbosa, a Policlínica Municipal ficou temporariamente sem telefone fixo e internet devido durante a manhã devido a danos causados por um raio.

Os serviços foram normalizados na parte da tarde.

Procurada pela reportagem, a Cemig informou que ainda não tinha os dados de incidência de raios que atingiram a cidade e que há como os moradores entrarem com pedido de ressarcimento de danos.

As informações sobre os procedimentos podem ser obtidas no site da concessionária de energia.

Nesta semana, o g1 mostrou que a incidência de raios em Juiz de Fora aumenta 68% em 2026 . Até outubro, foram 88.549 descargas elétricas na cidade, que fica a aproximadamente 20km de Matias Barbosa. Os dados são do Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas Espaciais (Inpe).

O pesquisador do Inpe Kleber Naccarato explicou que Juiz de Fora faz parte de uma região que, historicamente, registra maior incidência desses fenômenos.

"A região é montanhosa. Você tem a confluência de serras, tanto no norte do Rio de Janeiro quanto no leste do estado de São Paulo. Então, esse relevo montanhoso é um dos responsáveis por uma atividade de raios maior. Como você tem a proximidade do oceano, muitas frentes frias chegam a essa região”.

Ele ressalta que esses efeitos têm se intensificado ao longo dos anos, gerando impactos cada vez maiores à medida que as mudanças climáticas avançam.

"As mudanças climáticas estão aquecendo o planeta. O efeito do El Niño de 10 anos atrás não é o mesmo do efeito hoje. Isso porque estamos tornando a atmosfera mais quente. O planeta Terra está ficando cada vez mais propício a eventos extremos e mais intensos."

articles.title: 2.800 tropas europeias fazem exercício militar inédito na Polônia | G1
articles.standfirst: Fora da OTAN, manobra liderada por França e Reino Unido mobiliza 2.800 militares para testar apoio à Ucrânia após eventual cessar-fogo.
articles.summary: Fora da OTAN, manobra liderada por França e Reino Unido mobiliza 2.800 militares para testar apoio à Ucrânia após eventual cessar-fogo.
articles.body:
Fora da OTAN , manobra liderada por França e Reino Unido mobiliza 2.800 militares para testar apoio à Ucrânia após eventual cessar-fogo.

Milhares de tropas europeias estão participando de um exercício militar sem precedentes no sudeste da Polônia para se preparar para uma possível missão pós-guerra na Ucrânia, com o objetivo de ajudar a estabilizar o país e reconstruir suas forças armadas assim que o conflito terminar.

Tropas europeias de 11 países realizam exercício militar na Polônia para possível missão pós-guerra na Ucrânia, perto da fronteira da Polônia com a Ucrânia, descrevendo o episódio como provavelmente uma provocação intencional de Moscou sincronizada com os exercícios.

O local da queda do míssil fica a cerca de 75 quilômetros (47 milhas) da área de treinamento.

Liderada pela França e pelo Reino Unido, a força multinacional é uma iniciativa militar fora do âmbito da OTAN da chamada Coalizão dos Dispostos (Coalition of the Willing), um grupo político mais amplo formado por 37 nações que apoiam a Ucrânia.

O exercício de duas semanas, que começou em 9 de novembro, testa pela primeira vez a capacidade dessa coalizão de se mobilizar na Ucrânia após o fim da guerra. A iniciativa visa tanto testar planos de deslocamento quanto enviar uma mensagem à Rússia e ao governo Trump de que os países europeus estão assumindo um protagonismo militar maior.

Aliados europeus se unem em apoio à Ucrânia

Líderes da Ucrânia e de quase outras 40 delegações reuniram-se em Berlim na quinta-feira para reforçar o apoio a Kiev e discutir os arranjos de segurança da Ucrânia no pós-guerra.

O presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelensky , quer garantir que a Rússia não volte a invadir o país. Moscou, por sua vez, quer manter a OTAN afastada de suas fronteiras.

Foto de líderes europeis em cúpula da Coalizão dos Dispostos. — Foto: Markus Schreiber/AP

O enviado dos EUA, Jared Kushner , disse na quinta-feira acreditar que a Rússia esteja “confortável” com garantias de segurança semelhantes às da OTAN para a Ucrânia no pós-guerra.

Ele e o também enviado norte-americano Steve Witkoff estiveram em Berlim para tranquilizar os líderes europeus sobre as discussões do presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump , a respeito do fim da guerra — que já dura quase cinco anos — durante suas históricas conversas trilaterais na quinta-feira com o líder russo, Vladimir Putin , e o presidente chinês, Xi Jinping , na China.

Trump participou por telefone das negociações em Berlim após sua reunião com Putin, segundo Kushner.

A Ucrânia busca há muito tempo ingressar na OTAN, especialmente pela garantia de defesa mútua prevista no Artigo 5 da aliança, segundo o qual um ataque a um membro é considerado um ataque a todos. Não ficou imediatamente claro que formato essas eventuais garantias de segurança teriam, nem se a Rússia e a Ucrânia acabariam por aceitá-las.

Após a reunião de quinta-feira, o chanceler alemão, Friedrich Merz , afirmou que o exercício na Polônia mostra que a “Coalizão dos Dispostos está pronta para contribuir, junto aos Estados Unidos da América, para assegurar a paz”.

Enviado dos EUA para assuntos externos, Steve Witkoff, fala ao ouvido do presidente ucraniano, Volodymyr Zelensky em reunião em Berlim. — Foto: Markus Schreiber

Força multinacional ajudaria a reestruturar as forças armadas da Ucrânia

Cerca de 2.800 militares da Bélgica, Estônia, França, Alemanha, Lituânia, Países Baixos, Espanha, Suécia e Reino Unido participam do exercício, com a Polônia fornecendo o suporte logístico. A Turquia participou remotamente a partir de Istambul.

O presidente francês, Emmanuel Macron , afirmou na quinta-feira que 1.100 soldados da França foram mobilizados e que “temos operações terrestres, aéreas e também marítimas, com uma dúzia de países atuando nesta coalizão”.

O exercício na Polônia ocorre após 12 meses de planejamento da Força Multinacional-Ucrânia (MNF-U), segundo o brigadeiro britânico Campbell Close, vice-comandante de operações da 1ª divisão do Exército Francês — divisão responsável pelo componente terrestre do exercício “Koalicja” na Polônia.

“Este é um exercício de deslocamento”, disse Close na segunda-feira, no campo de treinamento militar de Nowa Deba, no sudeste da Polônia. “Somos uma força defensiva.”

Ele elogiou a condução logística da Polônia na movimentação de milhares de veículos, militares e equipamentos para as manobras.

Caso seja enviada após a entrada em vigor de um cessar-fogo, a força ajudaria a reconstruir as forças armadas da Ucrânia, forneceria a segurança necessária para reabrir o espaço aéreo do país e auxiliaria na remoção de minas no Mar Negro, afirmou o tenente-general Tom Bateman, comandante da MNF-U. A missão não teria funções de manutenção ou monitoramento da paz.

Soldados praticaram defesa antidrones e testaram novos equipamentos

As tropas da coalizão chegaram à Polônia por mar, ar e terra, informou o governo polonês, antes de seguirem por ferrovia e rodovia até a área de treinamento de Nowa Deba.

Os militares ensaiaram o transporte de pessoal e equipamentos, realizaram exercícios conjuntos de comando e controle e operaram caças e uma aeronave de reabastecimento aéreo. Também utilizaram drones de vigilância, treinaram respostas a ataques com drones e praticaram guerra de trincheiras.

A ideia inicial da Coalizão dos Dispostos era oferecer à Ucrânia garantias de segurança semelhantes às do Artigo 5 da OTAN. Diante da falta de compromisso da OTAN em assumir essa função, França e Reino Unido decidiram avançar com os planos de uma proposta europeia separada, reunindo países dispostos a socorrer a Ucrânia caso necessário.

No ano passado, Putin declarou que quaisquer tropas estrangeiras em território ucraniano seriam consideradas “alvos legítimos”.

Embora as tropas multinacionais possam ter uma função puramente defensiva, ainda assim precisariam atuar como uma “força de combate para sua própria proteção”, avaliou Ed Arnold, pesquisador associado sênior do centro de estudos militares RUSI, em Londres .

articles.title: Pontins fined £1m after grandmother's death at Brean Sands resort
articles.summary: A grandmother died after a part of an air conditioning duct and ceiling collapsed onto guests.
articles.body:
Pontins holiday park resort has been fined £1m after a grandmother died in a "catastrophic incident" that was "an accident waiting to happen", a judge ruled.

Wendy Jones, 68, of Hereford, died six months after a 40m (131ft) section of air conditioning duct and ceiling collapsed onto guests at Pontins' Brean Sands resort, Somerset, in February 2019.

On Friday, Pontins' parent firm, Britannia Jinky Jersey, was sentenced at Bristol Crown Court to pay a £1m fine.

Jones' son James Havard-Jones said: "There is a temptation to describe what happened as an accident. I cannot do that. An accident is something unforeseeable. This was not unforeseeable. This was preventable."

Contractor Stephen Bennison also received a 10-month prison sentence, suspended for 18 months.

They both admitted failure to discharge a duty under health and safety laws.

During sentencing, Judge Neil Moody said Bennison was contracted to work on the ceiling because he was cheaper than other bids.

Bennison then subcontracted to untrained individuals and failed to carry out a risk assessment, which Judge Moody described as a serious failing.

"It was an accident waiting to happen. Cutting costs at expense of safety was a factor," he said.

The court heard on Thursday that Bennison carried out work on the ceiling despite not being a qualified structural engineer.

He ordered more slabs than were needed and it was agreed Bennison would put the leftover slabs on top of the ventilation ducting, the court was told.

The prosecution added that "the whole job was done without proper planning on either side" . They said it showed the parent company "put profits over safety".

Jones was one of the 18 people injured during the incident which unfolded ahead of a bingo game.

Havard-Jones said in a statement after the trial that the fine is "substantial and should serve as a lesson to other companies that they have to behave properly".

"My Mum's life was cut short because of the incompetence and negligence of others.

"It's been seven long years of anxiety, stress and worry."

Jones' daughter Hayley Kendall added: "Nothing will ever replace the loss of our mum.

"No-one should ever have to go through what we went through as a family."

Det Supt Roger Doxsey, senior investigating officer at Avon and Somerset Police, said the "catastrophic incident lasted a mere matter of seconds", but its consequences are still "painfully felt" seven years on.

"Wendy's family are absolutely right when they say this incident was entirely preventable.

"It is a minor miracle, given the weight of the ducting, the nature of its collapse, and the volume of other people present in the Fun Factory at the time of the incident, that more people were not seriously injured and killed," Doxsey added.

The ruling follows an investigation from BBC News, which exposed how a former site manager at Brean Sands raised concerns at the time that the insulation had been unsafely installed and told Pontins' head office he feared the ceiling would collapse.

Brean Sands and Pakefield in Suffolk are currently under contract to house construction workers building Hinkley Point C and Sizewell nuclear plants.

Britannia, which bought Pontins out of receivership in 2011, also runs more than 60 hotels across England, Wales and Scotland.

articles.title: TikTok influencer Luke Hamnett's 'surreal' visit to Number 10
articles.summary: Luke Hamnett says he managed to film himself mimicking the famous dance from film Love Actually.
articles.body:
An influencer has spoken of his "surreal" visit to Downing Street to interview the prime minister and mimic the famous dance from the film Love Actually.

Luke Hamnett, who has about 1.3 million followers on TikTok, spoke to Andy Burnham at Number 10 for an episode of his Live, Laugh, Luke podcast.

The pair covered a mixture of topics, including music, tattoos, Larry the Cat, the NHS, the cost of living crisis and the safety of the LGBTQIA+ community.

Hamnett, from Stoke-on-Trent, said he was "very proud" to have spoken to Burnham "about causes and subjects close to my heart".

"It really was a pinch-me moment to be honest," he added. "A working-class man from Stoke, walking through the famous Downing Street door with my parents, is something I'll never forget."

The former insurance salesman, who started his content creation career by posting comic videos during lockdown, said he was nervous initially but quickly "relaxed into it".

Hamnett told BBC Radio Stoke: "Because we had a limited time, I had to make sure I was focused and moving it onto the next section... It was a surreal moment to be honest."

Asked what it was like being at Number 10, he said: "I did the Love Actually dance where I was dancing through Downing Street.

"I don't understand how that happened but I'm here for it."

The famous scene from the film features Hugh Grant's character, the prime minister David, dancing through the rooms and hallways of Number 10 along to Girls Aloud's song Jump.

The video of Hamnett recreating the dance has since been posted on TikTok and garnered more than 150,000 views so far.

Hamnett also said he was shocked at how expensive some of the furniture was, revealing that he was told some of the chairs he was moving around were worth about £400,000.

"If I broke that chair, I would've had to sell my mum… £400,000 a chair and I was slamming them down like it was no-one's business," he said.

Among the subjects he and Burnham spoke about was Stoke-on-Trent and which region it was in, with Hamnett adamant that it was in the North West, despite it officially being in the West Midlands.

But he said one of the most important things to him was ensuring the questions he asked were answered.

"I basically said that everyone is sick of a political answer," he added. "If you ask a question, people beat about the bush but we want answers."

articles.title: From Chocolate Peppermint Puppy Chow to Creamy Cheesecake: Joy Bauer’s Make-Ahead Thanksgiving Treats
articles.summary: These three desserts, Chocolate Peppermint Puppy Chow, Mini Cheesecakes and Crispy Cranberry Cookies, can be made ahead of time, making holiday hosting less stressful and a lot more fun.
articles.body: Join our 75-Day Walking Challenge and get Joy Bauer’s weekly meal plan for FREE in the Start TODAY app. My favorite moment on Thanksgiving comes after the dinner plates are cleared, and somebody asks, “Should we put on coffee?” That’s my cue to bring out dessert. All of these treats can be made ahead (hello, stress-free hosting), and according to my family, you’ll want to try all three! Easy Mini Cheesecakes Peel back the paper liner and you’ve got a perfectly portioned cheesecake all to yourself, graham cracker crust and all. I blend light cream cheese with part-skim ricotta for a silky, creamy filling with a hint of fresh lemon. Baking them in a muffin tin makes them easy to prep ahead and pass around. Then comes the fun part: set out a toppings bar and let everyone dress their own. Think: whipped cream, fresh berries, mini chocolate chips, a sprinkling of crushed grahams ... or even chopped nuts. And if pumpkin is a must at your table, my pumpkin cheesecake deserves a spot, too. In my house, two kinds of cheesecake is very easy sell! Peppermint Pistachio Puppy Chow Fair warning: This stuff is hard to stop snacking on. Rice Chex get a glossy coat of melted chocolate and peanut butter (or any preferred nut butter), then crunchy pistachios and crushed candy canes add a festive flair and amazing flavor. I stir some of the pistachios and candy into the mix and scatter the rest on top while the chocolate’s still soft. Once it sets in the fridge, break it into clusters. I save a few big ones for quality control, obviously! Serve it on Thanksgiving, then make another batch for holiday movie nights or spoon it into jars to give as gifts. Crispy Cranberry Pecan Granola Cookies You know that extra-good piece of granola with a toasted nut and a bit of dried fruit stuck to it? I wanted a whole cookie like that. Rolled oats pressed thin give these crisp edges, and buttery pecans and sweet-tart cranberries are tucked into every bite. Almond butter holds it all together, and a touch of maple syrup adds toasty sweetness. My dad and I like ours crispy … but if you prefer a softer middle, just press them a little thicker and pull them from the oven a few minutes early.

articles.title: Trump, Putin, Xi pledge to increase global petrol supplies – but how?
articles.summary: Analysts are sceptical about how this will be achieved amid the ongoing wars in Ukraine and Iran.
articles.body:
The United States, China and Russia have pledged to increase petrol supplies as the wars in Iran – started by Israel and the US – and Ukraine – started by Russia – continue to upend global energy markets.

Following their trilateral summit in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday, US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russia’s President Vladimir Putin said in a joint statement that they “plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations”.

The three leaders also “reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows”.

But analysts are sceptical about how this will actually work amid the US having little to no spare refining capacity, Russia being constrained by continued Ukrainian attacks on its energy infrastructure and China’s crude oil imports disrupted by the US and Israel’s war on Iran.

“The trilateral statement should be treated as political noise rather than the first step to boosting global fuel supplies,” Hamad Hussain, a senior climate and commodities economist at Capital Economics, told Al Jazeera.

“The announcement sounds like it is designed to placate consumers and constituencies. Previous efforts to increase supply [like the US-Russian diesel deal] went nowhere,” Frederic Schneider, a nonresident senior fellow at the Middle East Council on Global Affairs, told Al Jazeera.

So is what the three leaders said impossible?

How big are these countries’ refineries?

China and the US are the world’s biggest oil refiners by capacity, followed by Russia and India.

China has roughly 18.5 to 18.83 million barrels per day (bpd) of oil refining capacity. But refining in the country is dependent on its crude oil imports, which have been badly disrupted by the continuing US-Iran conflict in the Strait of Hormuz, through which Gulf oil exporters normally ship crude oil – much of it to Asia.

According to a November report by the US Energy Information Administration (EIA), crude oil refinery imports in China fell by 2.1 million bpd in the second quarter of 2026 and by an additional 0.8 million barrels bpd in the third quarter of the year.

As of January 1 this year, the US had an operable crude oil distillation capacity of about 18.16 million bpd. Production has increased since the war began, and is already running at near full capacity.

According to an October EIA report, “the US refinery fleet has run at higher-than-normal rates this year, with refinery utilisation averaging more than 95 percent of capacity between May and September, the highest for those months since 1998”.

Russia has roughly 6.5 million bpd of oil refining capacity, according to the International Energy Agency.

But Ukrainian drone strikes on its energy infrastructure have severely impacted its refining capacity. “In June, Russian refinery throughput fell to 3.8 million barrels per day, its lowest level in more than 20 years and roughly 30 percent below a year earlier,” a September International Energy Agency report noted.

Meanwhile, India has an oil refining capacity of about 5.36 million bpd, according to government figures. But New Delhi is also heavily dependent on crude oil imports, and this has been affected by blockades in the Strait of Hormuz.

According to the EIA, US refineries are currently running at close to maximum capacity.

This has been driven largely by “tight global supplies for distillate fuel oil, leading to high international demand for US distillate fuel oil exports”, a November EIA report states. Distillate fuel oil is refined petroleum which includes diesel fuels and light fuel oils.

Hussain said that while it may be profitable to refine more oil amid higher oil prices this year, the issue is that Washington “does not have spare capacity” to do so.

The Trump administration says it is determined to boost global fuel supply and US Energy Secretary Chris Wright has said his department is “talking about reopening every refinery we can” to do so.

According to a November 19 Reuters report, US refiner Valero Energy agreed to buy the century-old LyondellBasell Industries refinery near Houston, Texas, in October and restore a portion of the facility, adding 165,000 bpd of processing capacity by the end of 2027.

The plan would reverse years of refinery closures in the US and add about 1 percent to overall US refining capacity of 18 million bpd, Reuters reported. But analysts say the total price tag of acquiring and recommissioning this refinery could reach $1bn.

Since last year, long-range Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil refineries have resulted in serious fuel shortages across the country.

According to the IEA, in the first eight months of 2026, a Russian refinery was hit on average once every three days.

Reuters has reported that drone attacks have slashed Russian oil refineries’ combined crude processing volumes by 45 percent since late October and several regions have also begun limiting fuel.

On Friday, Reuters also reported that the Russia-installed governor of Crimea’s Sevastopol region, Mikhail Razvozhayev, said petrol sales there were being limited to one full car tank and 20 litres (5.3 gallons) in jerrycans at a number of pumping stations from Thursday.

He said the measures were being introduced to prevent people from filling canisters with hundreds of litres at a time, causing queues and preventing others from refilling.

The Siberian city of Tomsk also capped sales of petrol and diesel to 30 and 50 litres, respectively, from last week, according to local authorities.

On Thursday, the city of Penza, 770km (480 miles) southeast of Moscow, restricted petrol sales to 50 litres while limiting diesel to 200 litres per vehicle. At least half a dozen other regions introduced restrictions earlier this month.

With Ukrainian attacks continuing and Russia limiting fuel, refining more is currently a challenge for the country.

According to a November EIA report, Russia is also a major fuel exporter, especially of diesel. So any issues with its refining and decline in its exports will have a global impact.

While Trump and Putin agreed on a deal in October to allow some Russian diesel exports, none of the shipped fuel has reached customers, as traders have refused to take it .

The EIA noted that Russia’s loss of refinery operations has also “reduced refining activity in Asia and the Middle East, contributing to diesel prices increasing to the highest nominal levels on record in September”.

The conflict in the Strait of Hormuz strained crude oil imports to China earlier this year, but these have largely recovered.

While Beijing does not officially disclose the volumes of crude flowing into or out of its strategic and commercial stockpiles, Reuters reported that the world’s largest crude importer saw arrivals of 9.88 million bpd in October, up 9.4 percent from September’s 9.03 million bpd and the most since March, just after the war began.

Before the Iran war began on February 28, China was purchasing an average of 10.5 million barrels of crude per day by sea, according to sea-borne commodity data group Vortexa .

China also began stockpiling crude oil in October as imports recovered.

According to Hussain, “China does have some spare refinery capacity it could utilise”.

“But given that petrol and diesel inventories appear to be low in China, any increase in refined output may be used to replenish reserves rather than for export, which would keep global fuel supply constrained,” he said.

“In any case, the return of refined output from the Middle East will be key to lowering global fuel prices,” he added.

articles.title: Spain court grants bail to pro-Palestinian activist James ‘Fergie’ Chambers
articles.summary: Chambers left Aranjuez prison near Madrid on Friday afternoon, shortly after Spain’s High Court ordered him released.
articles.body:
A court in Spain has granted conditional bail to James “Fergie” Chambers, a pro-Palestine philanthropist who is the subject of an ongoing extradition request by the United States government.

Chambers left Aranjuez prison near Madrid on Friday afternoon, shortly after Spain’s High Court ordered him released. Speaking to journalists outside the prison, Chambers thanked his supporters.

“I got letters from all over the place these past months. People who don’t know me across Spain,” he told reporters. “I am grateful for the people of this country”.

Chambers said his mother was visiting him in the prison today when they were told, saying “we were sitting and eating some cookies and the guards knocked on my door and said give us five minutes we have some good news for you”. He said it was a “sweet moment” finding out he was going to be released while his mother was visiting him and that he will now have time with his mother who is visiting Spain, adding “this is very special,” said Chambers.

Chambers’s legal team described the bail release as “wonderful news”.

“My client has been imprisoned for nearly five months without having been convicted of any crime, and in the absence of credible evidence to support the US charges. We hope the National Court will reject this baseless extradition request,” said Aitor Martinez, Chambers’s lawyer, in a statement.

The US government’s case centres on Chambers’s alleged laundering of $7.5m, which he is said to have wired several years ago from a US bank account to Tunisia, where he lived at the time, allegedly using the cash to support Hamas. He is not charged with any “terrorism” offences and denies any wrongdoing.

Chambers’ wife Stella Schnabel said: “Today is an enormous relief. After nearly five months of only being able to see Fergie through a pane of glass during prison visits, and our five year old son asking every day where his dad is, we can finally be together as a family. Nothing can undo what we have endured, or the time Fergie has lost with our son, but at least we can now be together.

“But we still have a cloud of uncertainty hanging over us. Fergie faces the threat of extradition to the US, where he risks up to 30 years in prison for his solidarity with the Palestinian people. Our baby is due in March, and we have no idea whether Fergie will be by my side when our baby is born or whether he will be in a US supermax prison.”

In a recent legal development, lawyers for Chambers said mistranslations between the US criminal charge in English and the version presented to Spanish authorities in Spanish made the allegations seem more serious.

After a hearing last week, the court had been expected to rule on the extradition request in the coming weeks, but it said on Friday that the translation errors could delay a final decision.

The High Court said it had decided to release Chambers after US authorities acknowledged what they described as substantial and unintentional errors in the Spanish translation of an FBI agent’s sworn statement, submitted in support of the extradition request.

“The US authorities’ admission that they made ‘substantial’ changes to the extradition documents when translating them into Spanish raises grave concerns that the evidence was manipulated to mislead the Spanish authorities about the seriousness of the allegations against my client,” said Martinez.

“This further demonstrates why the UN Special Rapporteur on Human Rights Defenders has warned that Fergie would face ‘irreparable human rights violations’ if extradited to the US and has called for the extradition request to be rejected.”

Chambers, the heir to the Cox Enterprises media fortune and worth a reported $250m, was arrested on an Interpol Red Notice in Ibiza in July, but has since applied for asylum in Spain.

He cannot be extradited until the asylum claim is resolved, and if it is successful, he cannot be extradited from Spain to the US at all.

Chambers’s wife, Stella Schnabel, previously told Al Jazeera that she was appealing to Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez to intervene on their behalf and grant an expedited asylum request.

“If [Sanchez] chooses not to act, he risks enabling [US President Donald] Trump to establish a precedent in Spain and across Europe which criminalises solidarity with the Palestinian people,” she said.

Additional reporting by Graham Keeley in Madrid

articles.title: River Tweed trail starting to unlock 'spectacular landscapes'
articles.summary: The River Tweed Trail from Moffat to Berwick-upon-Tweed is expected to be completed by 2028.
articles.body:
A multi-million pound trail along the 113-mile (181km) route of the River Tweed is starting to unlock its "spectacular landscapes".

The route running from Moffat near the river's source to Berwick-upon-Tweed is due to be completed in 2028.

It is at the heart of the wider Destination Tweed tourism and river restoration project.

Two new footbridges have just been put in place that will help walkers access the "landscapes, nature, history, culture and communities" of the Scottish Borders near Tweedsmuir.

Bid launched to unearth river's hidden history

River Tweed trail aims to rival city attractions

The trail starts in Dumfries and Galloway and then runs through the Borders and North Northumberland.

The aim is to create a "major new tourism asset" for the area.

Jenny Linehan, Scottish Borders Council's (SBC's) executive member for the environment, said it was a "welcome step forward" in the plan.

"We want to make it easier for residents and visitors to enjoy our countryside and lead healthier lifestyles through active travel, with more opportunities to walk and cycle as the route develops," she said.

The trail is being developed by SBC in partnership with the Tweed Forum, Dumfries and Galloway Council and Northumberland County Council.

Its delivery is being managed by Turner and Townsend and funding for the trail includes £10m from the Scottish government through the Borderlands Growth Deal.

The new structures at Benshaw Burn and Logan Burn have been installed at the sites of former railway bridges on the historic Edinburgh to Talla rail route.

Although the original bridges were removed, their stone abutments and wingwalls remain.

Luke Fisher, Tweed Forum's Destination Tweed project director, said it was an important step in bringing the trail to life and "making some of the area's most beautiful landscapes more accessible to walkers and visitors".

He said they hoped to create a "lasting asset" delivering benefits for communities while also "celebrating and protecting the special environment surrounding the river".

River Tweed trail lands £3m funding support
